language.script: Thai (with occasional Lanna/Tai Tham script on cultural signage)
language.sample_text: ระวัง — งานก่อสร้างถนน
language.script_notes: Standard Thai script nationally; the historic Lanna (Tai Tham) script appears decoratively on temple signage and cultural sites in Chiang Mai, visually distinct from standard Thai.
false_friends: Laos (shared northern mountains and Buddhist architecture)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: More common on winding mountain roads.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Dramatic switchback mountain roads are common.

architecture.roof_style: Distinctive Lanna-style temple roofs — multi-tiered, steeply pitched, with elaborately carved wooden gables and 'kalae' crossed-horn decorations on rooftops.
architecture.roof_material: Wood-shingle or clay tile on traditional Lanna buildings; corrugated metal on modern houses.
architecture.wall_construction: Traditional Lanna wooden houses on stilts with crossed 'kalae' decorative gable finials; Chiang Mai's old city retains a walled, moated layout with numerous temples.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Dark carved teak wood tones on traditional Lanna buildings; gold and white on Lanna temples.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Lanna-style temples with carved wooden roofs and naga (serpent) staircases; the walled and moated Chiang Mai old city; hill-tribe villages on the surrounding mountains; Doi Suthep hilltop temple.

nature.vegetation: Dense tropical monsoon and montane forest covers the mountainous terrain, with terraced rice paddies and increasingly cooler-climate crops at higher elevation.
nature.terrain: Thailand's most mountainous region — high mountains and narrow valleys, including Doi Inthanon (2,565m, Thailand's highest peak) near Chiang Mai; steep, dissected ridges trending north-northeast to south-southwest.
nature.climate_signature: Noticeably cooler and more misty than the rest of Thailand at elevation; seasonal burning haze (dry season) is a recognizable regional atmospheric feature.

vehicles.plate_color: Province names such as Chiang Mai (เชียงใหม่) and Chiang Rai (เชียงราย) appear on the plate.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Red songthaews (shared pickup-truck taxis) are the iconic Chiang Mai transport — a distinctive regional tell.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coverage around Chiang Mai and along main mountain highways; sparser in remote hill-tribe areas.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar northern mountain terrain, Buddhist temple architecture, related Thai/Lao script families
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Thailand drives on the LEFT while Laos drives on the right; Thailand's infrastructure and road density are much more developed.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The north is mountainous with Lanna-style carved temples; central Thailand is flat rice-paddy plains, and the south is a rubber/palm-covered peninsula with visible mosques in the deep south.
